[Thinking]
**Analyzing sphere arrangement**

I need to reason out the positions of three equal spheres with a radius of 3 resting on the z=0 plane. They’re tangent to the plane and to each other. Their centers form an equilateral triangle at z=3. Their coordinates are at (0,0,3), (6,0,3), and the third center at (3,3√3,3). The tangency points between them lie along the lines connecting the centers. Overall, this arrangement forms a triangle shape, confirming my calculations.
[/Thinking]

Place the plane as \(z = 0\), and let each sphere have radius 3, so their centers are at height \(z = 3\).

Because each pair of spheres is tangent, the distance between any two centers is \(2 \times 3 = 6\). So the three centers form an equilateral triangle of side length 6 in a horizontal plane.

The tangency point between any two spheres lies on the line segment joining their centers, exactly midway between them (because the spheres are congruent and tangent). Thus the three pairwise tangency points are the midpoints of the sides of that equilateral triangle of centers.

The three midpoints of the sides of an equilateral triangle themselves form another equilateral triangle (just scaled down by a factor of 1/2), all in the same plane.

So, the new shape formed by the tangent points is an equilateral triangle.

**triangle**
